status: FROZEN BEFORE ANY OUTCOME. No policy has been trained or evaluated under any actuator channel.
supersedes: receipts/manifests/lucid_thermal_barrier_preregistration_20260903.json as the FIRST thing to try. That document stays valid for the thermal model itself, which remains the only route to an endogenous, accumulating constraint; it is no longer the first step because the deployment motivation behind it -- a motor that delivers less than its rating -- is obtainable directly from a parameter the simulator already has.
question: Is there a randomization channel and severity at which equal-budget DIRECT training does not reach the target, while a staged approach does? No channel measured so far has one, which is why no curriculum here has beaten fixed randomization.

why_the_actuator.observation: All six existing channels are properties of the robot's LOAD or of the WORLD: mass, torso centre of mass, ground material, a joint default-position offset, pushes, latency. None is a property of the actuator.
verified_gaps: The robot's URDF (gear_sonic/data/assets/robot_description/urdf/g1/main.urdf) contains ZERO <dynamics> tags, so no joint friction and no physical joint damping is declared for any joint. The simulated G1 has frictionless gearboxes; a real harmonic or planetary reducer does not, and is measurably stiffer cold than warm.

robots/g1.py sets effort_limit_sim to the URDF's PEAK rating and applies it forever. A deployed motor delivers less: the battery sags under load, the winding heats, and units vary. Unitree documents a derating strategy on the G1 that limits current when a joint passes its safe temperature.
The joint speed ceiling and the reflected inertia are likewise set once from motor specifications and never varied.
why_the_actuator.why_they_might_behave_differently: Two of these REMOVE CAPABILITY (a lower torque or speed ceiling) and one ADDS A NONSMOOTH TERM (static friction has a sign discontinuity at zero velocity, producing stiction and a deadband). The six existing channels do neither: they move a smooth parameter of a task the policy already solves. Whether that difference produces a learnability barrier is a measurement, not a claim.

the_risk_we_are_running.threat: Adding channels until a curriculum wins on one is fitting the benchmark to the method, and a win obtained that way means nothing.
mitigations: Each channel closes a nameable gap between this simulator and the target robot, verified in the asset rather than asserted.

The severity ladders are fixed in this document, before any outcome exists. A ladder may be rescaled ONCE on frozen-policy evidence from P0, because that is range-finding with no curriculum involved, and the rescaling must be recorded with its reason. After P1 begins, nothing moves.

The result is reported as a MAP. Every channel and severity at which direct training already reaches the target is reported as a place where a curriculum is unnecessary, and armature is included precisely because it is expected to be such a place.

A barrier requires BOTH that direct training fails AND that the target is reachable another way. A severity nothing reaches is an unlearnable task; the read-out already refuses to call that a candidate.

P0_frozen_policy_screen.what: five frozen policies x thirteen cells; tools/run_actuator_screen.sh
questions_in_order: is the channel live at all
is the top rung survivable by anyone
does it separate policies more than the baseline cell does
stop_rules: NOT LIVE: report it and check the run's own dr_scale_report before concluding anything physical. A channel that does nothing is a wiring result, not a physics result.
FLOOR at every rung: the ladder is too harsh; rescale once, on this evidence, and record it.
LIVE but does not separate policies: the channel measures difficulty and not capability. Report it and do not train on it.

P1_can_fixed_randomization_train_at_the_.what: four warm-start arms from the fixed@s8600 final, 1500 iterations, one seed, identical budget, environments, mixture and origin. Only the actuator channel's schedule differs.

arms.fixed_act_off: the actuator channels collapsed to nominal: the control that says what this budget buys with no new channel
arms.fixed_act_S: the channel pinned at the target severity for the whole run: DIRECT training at the target
arms.ramp_act_S: an open-loop schedule from nominal to S over the run: staged, with no feedback
arms.gate_act_S: the probe-gated curriculum expanding toward S: staged, with feedback

P1_can_fixed_randomization_train_at_the_.decides: whether direct training reaches the target, and whether staging is what makes the difference or merely the schedule
P1_can_fixed_randomization_train_at_the_.note: This is the comparison in the plain question 'can fixed DR train a good policy here'. fixed_act_S answers it; the other three say what the answer means.

P2_confirmation.what: the surviving contrast from scratch, paired on at least three seeds
P2_confirmation.decides: whether the P1 effect survives the 7.8-point between-seed effect this project has measured

frozen_decision_rules.C0_live: A channel enters P1 only if P0 finds it live (reference arm moves at least 5 points at the top rung) and survivable (some policy above 0.05 there).
frozen_decision_rules.C1_direct_training_fails: Direct training fails at severity S if fixed_act_S ends at least 10 points below fixed_act_off on the frozen held-out band. Smaller than that is a cost, not a failure.
frozen_decision_rules.C2_the_target_is_reachable: S is reachable if any staged arm (ramp_act_S or gate_act_S) ends within 5 points of fixed_act_off. Without this, C1 alone means the task is unlearnable at S and the finding is reported that way.
frozen_decision_rules.C3_a_barrier_exists: C1 AND C2. This is the first regime in this project where a curriculum could be necessary rather than optional.
frozen_decision_rules.C4_does_feedback_add_anything: gate_act_S must beat ramp_act_S by at least 5 points to credit feedback. A tie means the SCHEDULE crossed the barrier and the feedback did not, which is a result about staging, not about our controller.
frozen_decision_rules.C5_report_the_unnecessary_region: Every channel and severity where direct training reaches the target is reported as a place a curriculum is not needed.
frozen_decision_rules.C6_exposure_is_stated: Every arm reports realized exposure per severity band in environment-iterations, never episodes, and never the intended schedule.
frozen_decision_rules.C7_one_seed_screens: P1 is one seed. No superiority language until P2. The between-seed effect on absolute capability here is 7.8 points, larger than the C4 margin.

what_would_make_us_stop: P0 finds no live, survivable, separating channel: the actuator direction ends and the paper stays the failure analysis.
P1 finds direct training reaches the target everywhere: there is no barrier, and that is the map.
P1 finds nothing reaches the target: the severity is unlearnable, which is reported and not relabelled.
